findings.issue: Each Instance object carries a key `instance_details`, which the schema digest does not declare for the Instance class. Instance accepts only `counts`, `data_substrate`, `data_topic`, `instance_type`, `label`, `label_description`, `missing_information`, `notes`, `sampling_strategies`, `source_caveats` (plus `id`, `used_software`). Inventing a key is prohibited (#380); the content belongs in `notes` or `label_description`. This will fail validation.

Grant objects carry keys `grant_number` and `grant_title`; the schema digest gives no required or accepted-key list for Grant, and these key names are not attested anywhere in the digest. The same shape recurs in funders[1] and funders[2]. If Grant does not declare `grant_number`/`grant_title`, these are invented keys and will fail validation.

The value `https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/11211616` is a resolver/landing-page URL used as an `id` (uriorcurie) for a grant. This is a project page for the award, not an identifier minted for a part of this dataset, and the bundle supplies the award number (1OT2OD032742-01) rather than a registry identifier. Either omit the id or, if a label is needed, do not use an external landing page as the identity of the grant entity.

Nine creators without ORCIDs in the bundle are given minted fragment identifiers on the dataset DOI landing URL, e.g. `https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#creator-axelsson-u` (also fall-j, chinn-b, johannesson-a, khaliq-h, muralidharan-m, pan-e, polacco-b, zhang-y). A person has a referent outside this record, so the identifier must come from the evidence or be omitted; the bundle supplies no identifier for these people. Additionally no other value in the record points at these fragments, so they are not serving as labels. Omit `id` for these nine creators.

Person objects carry an `email` key. The schema digest does not attest `email` as a Person slot; no Person key list is given. If Person does not declare `email` this is an invented key. The email addresses are attested in the bundle and can be carried in `notes` on the parent object if Person cannot hold them.

Organization objects carry a `name` key; the schema digest supplies no accepted-key list for Organization, so `name` is unverified against the digest. This affects ~45 affiliation objects plus data_governance-adjacent Organization uses. If Organization does not declare `name`, all affiliations fail validation.

Each DatasetRelationship object carries a `description` key alongside the required `relationship_type` and `target_dataset`. DatasetRelationship accepts the same slots as the top-level Dataset listing, which does include `description`, so this is admissible — but the `description` values here describe the *target* dataset, not the relationship, and the target is already identified by `target_dataset`. Lower confidence than the other high findings; flagged for review rather than certain defect.

`publisher` is declared `uriorcurie`. The value `https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu` is a bare host URL, not an identifier for the publishing organization. The bundle names the publisher as University of Virginia Dataverse / University of Virginia and supplies ROR:0153tk833 for the University of Virginia (used elsewhere in this record). Either use the attested CURIE or omit; a bare hostname identifies no registered entity.

The record `id` is `https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C`, the DOI resolver URL. The `doi` slot correctly carries the bare `10.18130/V3/HIGT4C`. For a `uriorcurie` slot where a `doi:` prefix is available and is in fact used elsewhere in this record (version_access.latest_version_doi: `doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C`; related_datasets target_dataset values), the resolver form here creates two identities for one thing. Inconsistent with the record's own usage.

Value `Niestroy, Justin` is transcribed from the Dataverse `Depositor` field. `created_by` asks for the person or organization primarily responsible for creating the resource; the depositor is the person who uploaded the deposit. The bundle distinguishes Depositor from Author and from Point of Contact. This conflates deposit with creation.

`2026-07-15T00:00:00Z` is taken from the publication date of the three immunofluorescence image files within the release, not from any stated dataset-level modification date. The bundle gives Publication Date 2026-06-17 for the release and per-file published dates of 2026-06-17 and 2026-07-15. Deriving a dataset-level last-updated timestamp from a file-level publication date is an inference the bundle does not state.

No creator carries `credit_roles`, yet the bundle's preprint states a detailed Contributions paragraph for the overlapping author set of the Nature paper and the CM4AI preprint describes module-level responsibilities (e.g. Krogan laboratory generated SEC-MS; Lundberg Lab generated IF images; Ideker is corresponding author). For the CM4AI release itself the bundle does not assign CRediT roles, so omission is defensible — flagged only to record that the omission was considered.

`conforms_to` is set to `RO-Crate` and `conforms_to_standard` to `RO_CRATE`. This is supported by the bundle ('packaged ... as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format'). However RO-Crate describes the *packaging* of the release metadata rather than the content standard of the imaging or mass-spectrometry data themselves. Defensible but worth noting: no imaging or waveform content standard (e.g. DICOM/BIDS) is claimed, correctly, since the bundle names none.

`total_file_count: 10` is populated but `total_size_bytes` is omitted, while seven of ten file_collections carry `total_bytes`. The three IF archives are displayed only in GB, so a complete aggregate cannot be computed — omission is correct — but the asymmetry is worth recording. The source_caveats already notes this; no repair required.

Seven `total_bytes` values are back-computed from Dataverse's rounded human-readable sizes (e.g. 113.3 KB -> 116019). These are derived precision the bundle does not state; a reader will take 116019 as an exact byte count. The source_caveats discloses the conversion, which mitigates but does not remove the over-precision.

`counts: 11739` is placed on the Instance whose `instance_type` is 'Single-cell CRISPRi perturbation transcriptional profile'. 11,739 is the number of *targeted genes* in the atlas, not the number of instances of that type. The Instance description asks for the count of instances. Mismatch between the slot's meaning and the value.

`status: Beta`. The bundle's release title carries '(Beta)' and the version is 2.0. The slot description gives examples 'draft, published, deprecated'. 'Beta' is attested in the source title so this is grounded, but it mixes a release-maturity label with what the slot describes as a publication-status vocabulary.

`2025-02-27T00:00:00Z` is the Dataverse 'Data Creation Date' and also the 'Deposit Date' for this and for the March 2025, June 2025 and October 2025 releases — the same date is carried forward unchanged across four distinct releases in the bundle. Transcribed faithfully, but it is unlikely to be the creation date of the June 2026 release content specifically. Worth a source_caveat.

`start_date: 2025-02-27` reuses the Dataverse Data Creation Date as a collection start. The bundle nowhere states when data collection began; the project period (2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31) is an award period, not a collection window. The `timeframe_details` text is honest about the provenance, but populating `start_date` from a metadata deposit field asserts a collection boundary the bundle does not support.
`language: en` is not stated anywhere in the bundle. It is a near-certain inference from the documentation being in English, but it is an inference rather than an attested fact. Marginal.

`is_tabular: false` is not stated in the bundle. It is inferable from the content types (images, mass-spec archives, sequence data), but the SEC-MS and Perturb-seq derived products are plausibly tabular. The single boolean cannot represent a mixed-modality release accurately.

All four InstanceAcquisition objects set `was_directly_observed: true` and leave `was_inferred_derived`, `was_reported_by_subjects`, `was_validated_verified` unset. The bundle does describe validation (e.g. antibody quality scored per HPA protocol; CRISPR screen data 'currently being QCed'), so `was_validated_verified` is arguably supported for the imaging acquisition. Omission is safe; noted only for completeness.

Omitted. The bundle describes reproducibility assessment of GPT-4 assembly naming via semantic similarity across five replicate runs (SapBERT), which is an analysis of annotation quality. This relates to the U2OS Nature work rather than to the CM4AI release content, so omission is defensible, but the labeling_strategies slot already draws on that same methods material — the record is inconsistent about how far it reaches into the Nature methods.

Omitted while `preprocessing_strategies` is populated from the MuSIC pipeline description. The bundle states CRISPR screen 'resulting data are currently being QCed' and describes AP-MS quality-control filters (1% protein-level FDR, minimum PSM and protein counts, CompPASS-Plus FDR filtering) — the latter in the Nature U2OS methods rather than for CM4AI. Consistent with the record's stated scoping decision; flagged for review.

Both omitted. The release has clear logical partitions by cell line and treatment condition (MDA-MB-468 untreated/paclitaxel/vorinostat; KOLF2.1J undifferentiated/NPC/neuron/cardiomyocyte), which are represented instead through `subpopulations` and `file_collections`. Defensible modeling choice, but `subsets` (DataSubset) is the slot whose description names 'demographic subgroups' and logical partitions; the condition structure arguably belongs there too.

Omitted at dataset level while `distribution_formats[0].access_urls` carries the Dataverse landing page. The bundle supplies an API access pattern (`https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/`) but no complete direct download URL, so omitting `download_url` is correct. Noted to confirm the omission was deliberate.

The `notes` value states project organization (three pillars, six modules, collaborating institutions). This is descriptive content about the producing project that could sit in `description`; `notes` is reserved for residual content after description and structured slots are used (#385). Minor placement question rather than a factual defect.

The dataset-level `source_caveats` is long and carries several distinct concerns (referent selection, the 563-vs-464 conflict, portal aggregate counts, the U2OS/Nature scoping decision, byte-size conversion). Each is legitimate trust commentary, but the byte-size and image-count items would sit better as `source_caveats` on the file_collections and instances they concern, closer to the values they qualify.

The keyword list is transcribed verbatim from Dataverse and includes 'AP-MS' and 'affinity purification' plus 'perturb-seq' and 'perturbation sequencing' and 'iPSC' and 'induced pluripotent stem cell' and 'NPC' and 'neural progenitor cell' and 'scRNAseq' and 'single-cell RNA sequencing' — five synonym pairs. Faithful transcription; no repair needed, but the redundancy is inherited rather than chosen.

summary: Audited the full record against the declared CM4AI bundle. The record's factual content is well grounded: the referent choice (June 2026 release, doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C) correctly follows the manifest's SUPERSEDED BY ranking, the 464-vs-563 image-count conflict between tier-1 and tier-5 releases is resolved toward the higher tier and disclosed, and the Nature U2OS cell map is correctly held apart from the CM4AI releases. No fabricated dataset facts were found. The serious problems are structural rather than factual. Six high-severity findings concern shape: an invented `instance_details` key on all three Instance objects (a certain validation failure under #380); `grant_number`/`grant_title` keys on Grant objects and `email` keys on Person objects and `name` on Organization, none of which the supplied digest attests; nine minted fragment identifiers on the dataset DOI standing in for creators who have real-world referents and no attested identifier, which the v5 rule forbids and which nothing in the record points at; and a landing-page URL used as a Grant `id`. Medium findings concern identifier form and inference: `publisher` holds a bare hostname where ROR:0153tk833 is already used elsewhere in the record; the record `id` uses the DOI resolver URL while `version_access.latest_version_doi` and every `target_dataset` use the `doi:` CURIE for the same object, so one thing is written two ways; `created_by` carries the Dataverse depositor rather than a creator; and `last_updated_on` is derived from a file-level publication date the bundle never presents as a dataset modification date. Low findings are mostly disclosed over-precision (byte counts back-computed from rounded displays), a count/slot mismatch (11,739 targeted genes placed in Instance.counts), and small inference-vs-attestation questions (`language`, `is_tabular`, `collection_timeframes.start_date` reusing a deposit date). Repair priority: remove the invented keys, drop the nine minted person identifiers, and reconcile the DOI and publisher identifier forms; these are the findings that block validation or create duplicate identities.
